_comment: Permissions for the backup job's IAM user. Replace YOUR-BUCKET, remove
this _comment key, and attach it as an inline policy.
It can write new objects under one prefix of one bucket. It cannot read
them back, cannot delete or overwrite anything, and cannot see any other
**No s3:DeleteObject, and no s3:GetObject.** Deletion belongs to the
lifecycle rules, so a leaked key cannot destroy the backup history — the
first thing ransomware looks for. Withholding read matters too: these
files contain every password hash and a full map of which state systems
hold which data, and a job that only writes has no reason to read.
Restoring is done by you, signed in as yourself, not by this user.
s3:PutObject is scoped to the object path; ListBucket is not granted at
all, because the AWS CLI does not need it for a single-file `cp`.
